html:
Chicora was the name of a Native land on the coast of what is now South Carolina, made famous in the 1500s by a legend of great wealth.

In 1521 Spanish slavers from Hispaniola raided the coast near Winyah Bay and carried off about 60 people. One captive, baptised Francisco de Chicora, learned Spanish and told stories of a rich country, which he called Chicora, to the Spanish court. His tales led Lucas Vázquez de Ayllón to found the colony of San Miguel de Gualdape on the coast in 1526; it failed within months, and Francisco escaped back to his people. The legend went on to draw French and Spanish ventures to the region for decades. The real people of the area included the Winyah, the Waccamaw and the Cusabo further south, in what became South Carolina.
sum: Chicora was the name of a Native land on the coast of what is now South Carolina, made famous in the 1500s by a legend of great wealth.
